description.narrative: Project Development Objective (PDO). The proposed project development objective is to strengthen the capacity of selected sector institutions to support the effective implementation of the Recipient's National Agriculture and Food Security Investment Plan (PNIASA).

The objective of the Agriculture Sector Support Project for Guinea is to strengthen the capacity of selected sector institutions to support the effective implementation of the Recipient's National Agriculture and Food Security Investment Plan (PNIASA). There are three components to the project, the first component being strengthening of sector management capacities. This component aims at building the capacity of the sector ministries, as well as the capacity of the Chamber of Agriculture and other sector entities, with a medium to long-term objective of establishing a sound institutional environment in support of PNIASA implementation and laying the groundwork for the future preparation for a SWAp. It is expected to lead to an increase in PNIASA?s physical and financial execution rate, help mitigate mismanagement risks and minimize transaction costs. The second component is the analytical support to PNIASA implementation. The aim of this component is to create an enabling environment and establish the required preparedness conditions for selected PNIASA programs. Finally, the third component is the project management and coordination. Project activities will be coordinated by a small Operational Coordination Unit (COD) headed by a Coordinator Delegate (CD) and consisting of a small number of staff (8) including a financial expert, an accountant, a procurement specialist, a monitoring and evaluation specialist, an administrative assistant and two drivers and messengers.

title.narrative: 2.1.2 The detailed plans (APDs) for feeder roads are updated

comment.narrative: <p>The updated master plan for rural roads (“schéma directeur d’aménagement des pistes Rurales dans les 33 préfectures de Guinée”) represents a major undertaking by the PASAG. It costed US$ 2.09 million (14% of total project cost), was commissioned to a consortium of three consulting companies. It consists of: (i) a comprehensive inventory and assessment of the entire network of rural roads of the country (29,300 km), the previous one dated 1989; (ii) a broad investment plan for the sub-sector; (iii) the revision of criteria for prioritized rehabilitation work (including agriculture potential, population benefitting, environmental and social impact, etc.; (iv) the identification of 1100 km for priority rehabilitation based on these criteria; (v) the preparation of summary and detailed design (avant projets sommaires et détaillés) for these 1100 km together with the preparation of the tender documents: done with good ownership.   800 Km of rural roads will be finance by the rural mobility and connectivity program.</p>

<p>Core1. Staff benefitting (with 20 percent of women): This indicator was fully surpassed (190 percent) with 21 percent of women. In total 2,843 staffs are trained, the initial target was 1,500 staffs for the 4 years of project implementation. Regarding thewomen, the target was slightly exceed. It was 15% at the end of September 2018 but the gap was completed during the 4th quarter of 2018 when the specify training was delivered to 361 women. Then, more than (51 percent) of the trained staffs come from the central structures against 44 percent of the deconcentrated structures. In additional, it should be noted that 13 percent of people who have benefited from training come from sectoral socio-professional organizations.</p>

title.narrative: 2.1.1 The detailed plans (APDs) for irrigated areas are prepared

comment.narrative:
<p>The restructuring describes two changes that were not actual changes: (i) the increase of physical targets for detailed plans from 4,000 to 6,000 ha of irrigated areas and from 600 to 1,100 km of feeder roads. However, the PAD was already targeted 6,000 ha of irrigated area. A master plan for irrigated agriculture was prepared by the project and delivered. It consists of a comprehensive assessment of water resources, irrigable areas (estimated at 909,000 ha) and estimates on the scope for developing these areas. This led to the prioritization of 6,000 ha based on cost benefit and social and environmental impact considerations. 1600 ha was currently rehabilitated through the PDAIG project.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: The sector ministries'investment budget aligned with the PNIASA's priorities

comment.narrative: <p>The Alignment of budgets with PNIASA was surpassed (99, 62 percent). The baseline estimates indicated that only 50 percent of budgets used to be aligned with PNIASA. A specific analysis was commissioned in 2018 and showed that the figure of 99.62 percent had been achieved. This is the result of the fact that MTEF was introduced by the project whereby budgets result from the MTEF, which are aligned with the PNIASAN</p>

title.narrative: The operational institutional frameworks for priority value chains is implemeted

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was discontinued as this study was part of the Deep Dive that was jointly done with IFC.  The Deep Dive was more comprehensive and the Operational institutional frameworks for priority VC was not funded under the this project.</p>

title.narrative: 2.2.2 The strategy to finance agriculture inputs and equipements (including e-vouher approach) is elaborated and adopted

comment.narrative:
<p><em>E -voucher : <strong>The project also conducted an analytical study , a new approach</strong> to the delivery of inputs to farmers .</em> <em>The Government’s input subsidy program to promote the adoption of improved technological packages is facing many shortcomings</em><em>. Poor targeting, inadequate quantity of inputs, lack of access improved seeds and extension services haveundermined</em><em> the expected results of the Government’s input subsidy program. Moreover, the program lacked adequate targeting and many farmers do not benefit from the subsidized agricultural inputs. This analytical work was used by the WAAPP project to implement an e voucher pilot in Guinea. </em><em>This ensures the good governance of the system by introducing full traceability, transparency and flexibility, therefore avoiding leakages and improving targeting to those in needs. At completion, 100,000 farmers had been enrolled and 20,000 vouchers for seeds and 5,000 vouchers for kits of inputs (seeds, fertilizers and phytosanitary products) had been successfully issued. The system will further expand from 8 to 13 prefectures (and from 100,000 to 300,000 farmers) with further financial resources.</em></p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: 2.2.1 The national inventory of land use is completed

comment.narrative:
<p><strong>The national inventory of land use is completed and transmitted to ANASA for exploitation under the National Census of Agriculture and Livestock (RNAE) which will be implemented by the PASAG through the collaborative effort to <em>Support the agricultural statistics (US$11.20 million - US$5.00 million from IDA and US$0.20 million from Government and US$6.00 million from AFD </em> providing parallel financial support and FAO providing technical assistance</strong>.</p>
<p> </p>

title.narrative: 1.2.1 The sector ministries and Chamber of Agricultures progress reports are prepared semi-annually

comment.narrative: <p>A major bottleneck to implementing NAIPs in Africa (and worldwide in countries with similar investment plans) is the absence of monitoring systems so that the NAIPs remain largely documents on the shelves given there is no system to review and report on progress. Project support enabled the establishment of the sector M & E system through the manual, the database and result based reporting. The half-yearly and annual reports are produced according to the harmonized format. For more efficacy and efficiency in the sector the project has allowed the production of a mapping of the portfolio of projects / programs of the sector.</p>

title.narrative: 1.1.2 Priority sub-sector regulatory and operational codes are updated

comment.narrative: <p>For more efficient the sector institutions 4 codes were  updated : (i) le code de l’élevage” (livestock); (ii) le “code pastoral” (pastoral code), and; (iii) le code de l’aquaculture (aquaculture), iv code de l 'environnement (environment). Livestock Code has been adopted and promulgated   by the gouvernement which provided the necessary legal framework in terms of management of pastoral areas, transhumance and relations with crop farmers, access to water points and better integration of livestock and agriculture</p>

title.narrative: 1.3.2 The sector ministries Annual Work Programs and Budgets (PTBAs) are approved according to the RBM/GAR

comment.narrative: <p>The capacity building enabled the actors to develop the Budgets / Programs and MTEFs of each Ministry in 2017, 2018 and 2019. The sectors ministries were trained on the development of the AWPBs by using the RBM since May 2017 by the ATI. The AWPBs were timely produced and validated (by the central and regional services) of the 4 sectoral ministries. An M&E  operational produced up to date data.</p>

title.narrative: 1.1.1 The sector ministries and Chamber of Agricultures institutional diagnosis is completed and validated

comment.narrative: <p>The institutional diagnostic of the sectoral ministries and the chamber of agriculture was completed in January 2017 and followed by actions to put the key recommendations (institutional, organizational and operational which are necessary the better functioning of each institution) in practice : (i) targeted trainings were conducted based on the findings of the diagnostic (planning, budgeting, procurement, monitoring and evaluation). An international technical assistance was hired to help the government implement those recommendations. One of key recommendation was to  the SWAP approach which was successfully implemented.</p>

title.narrative: 2.1.3 The master plan for pastoral areas is prepared and validated

comment.narrative: <p>The master plan for pastoral areas (schéma directeur pastoral) was approved in August 2018 and provides a comprehensive account of pastoral areas and investment requirements in terms of water supply, pastoral areas, feeding requirements and vaccination centers so as to optimize in a sustainable manner the use of pastoral resources in the country. It is complemented by the pastoral code (code pastoral) that provides the necessary legal framework in terms of management of pastoral areas, transhumance and relations with crop farmers, access to water points, etc</p>

title.narrative: Annual financial audit produced on time.
Medium Term Expenditures Framework for each ministry produced

comment.narrative:
<p>This target was achieved  (100%), 8 MTEFs were produced. This is a major contribution to the PDO: (i) at completion, the four ministries had acquired the capacity to produce the MTEFs which means to convert the PNIASAN into actionable ministry programs and budgets enabling them to implement their share of PNIASAN interventions. As such the four ministries were praised by the Ministry of finance as ahead of all the other sectors in implementing the new Government regulation related to public finance passed in 2012 (Loi Organique Relative aux Lois de Finances (LORLF)). While two other sectors had started preparing MTEFs (health and education), the ones of the agriculture sector were appreciated for their quality by the MoF. MTEFs are also seen by the ministries as a convincing advocacy tool to increase budget allocation to the agriculture sector. A rather direct consequence was contained in theletter dated 29 August 2018 to frame the 2019 budget addressed by the Prime Minister to the ministries of economy, finance, budget and planning. The instructions are to freeze or reduce important expenditures to the benefits of five ministries, including agriculture, livestock fisheries, education and health, i.e. those who have prepared MTEFs. In addition, the Prime ministry instructs the recipient ministries to take note of his commitment to the 10 percent budget allocation to the sector .The Ministry of Budget uses the rural MTEFs as a model for the MTEF for other ministerial departments in the country. The RBM units were set up within each ministry to ensure the sustainability of the production of the program budgets, A computer software to facilitate the preparationof MTEF by the actors of the ministries has been created and is operational. Finally, the MTEFs contributed to the improvement of governance and support to the agricultural sector.</p>
<p> </p>
